statement: The Smithsonian National Museum of the American Indian publicly presents a version of the White Buffalo Calf Woman pipe-giving story explicitly attributed to John Lame Deer in 1967, witnessing a named twentieth-century telling within Lakota sacred narrative transmission.

sources.citation: Smithsonian National Museum of the American Indian, Native Knowledge 360, 'Oceti Sakowin Homelands', public White Buffalo Calf Woman account attributed to John Lame Deer (1967), https://americanindian.si.edu/nk360/plains-belonging-homelands/oceti-sakowin
sources.author: John Lame Deer (attributed public telling) / NMAI
sources.access_note: Named narrator and 1967 attribution verified in a publicly shared educational account. No restricted ceremony descriptions are supplied; complete oral source edition and permissions not independently reviewed.

does_not_demonstrate: 1967 dates this recorded telling, not the story's inception or a sacred event in calendar history.
A single authorized public telling cannot be treated as the exclusive Lakota account.
Documentation of a sacred pipe story does not permit replicating restricted rituals or imposing a monotheism label.
adversarial_counter: Oral narratives can have multiple tribally situated versions; narrator and the historical context must remain attached to any derivative summary.
notes: Institutional-source audit. Scope: named public page and its content only; no tradition founding-year inference. Independent historical / community review required before status change.
